items.headline: Google confirms contact with Project Suncatcher TPU satellite in orbit
items.summary: A prototype satellite carrying four Google TPUs launched October 1 on SpaceX's Transporter-18 rideshare, and Google confirmed it is operating as expected; the research moonshot is testing whether space could one day host scalable machine-learning infrastructure.

items.headline: Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report: AI has shifted near-term advantage to attackers
items.summary: Microsoft's annual threat report finds the median time from vulnerability discovery to weaponization has fallen below 24 hours and that AI is industrializing spear-phishing, with all four major state-sponsored threat clusters now integrating AI into live operations.

items.headline: Cloudflare releases Clef and Clef-Flash, open-weight 'decision models'
items.summary: Cloudflare's first in-house trained models skip text generation entirely, instead running a single forward pass to return typed probabilities for agent decisions; the 27B Clef and 9B Clef-Flash are built on Qwen backbones and released under Apache 2.0 with far lower latency than comparable LLMs.

items.headline: OpenAI cuts ties with three safety researchers over mishandled sensitive information
items.summary: An internal OpenAI investigation found the researchers shared confidential material with a third-party AI safety organization outside approved channels; the move follows reporting that OpenAI executives had dismissed earlier employee warnings about safety practices.

items.headline: UCLA's light-powered optical chip detects deepfake video with ~98% accuracy
items.summary: A new optical-neural processor analyzes 15+ video streams simultaneously by exploiting the physical propagation of light rather than conventional digital processing, reporting 97.79% average detection accuracy; its speed and low power draw could help screen the growing flood of AI-generated video.

items.headline: Superfluid helium qubit design could cut quantum computing errors 100x
items.summary: University of Surrey researchers proposed the first superfluid-helium-based qubit (SHOQ), which is naturally immune to common electromagnetic noise; calculations predict error rates roughly 100 times lower than today's superconducting qubits, potentially easing a major barrier to scaling quantum computers.

items.headline: Robotics startup FieldAI reportedly raising $700M at a $10B valuation
items.summary: FieldAI's robot-navigation models work without maps, GPS, or pre-defined paths, significantly cutting deployment costs for field and industrial robots; the reported round would roughly reflect strong investor appetite for general-purpose robotics AI.

items.headline: Perplexity releases Decider v1, a 27B decision model
items.summary: Perplexity joins Cloudflare and TypeSafe in shipping a dedicated 'decision model' aimed at fast, structured agent decisions rather than open-ended text generation, reflecting a broader industry shift toward specialized small models for agentic workflows.

items.headline: OpenAI launches 'dots,' always-on agents powered by GPT-6 Astra
items.summary: Unveiled at OpenAI DevDay, dots are persistent agents that work from their own cloud computer and browser across 4,000+ connected apps, pursuing user-defined goals in the background with minimal supervision; the launch intensifies competition with Microsoft and Meta's own agent platforms.

items.headline: Amazon merges Ads Console and DSP into a single 'Amazon Ads Agent'
items.summary: Announced at Amazon's unBoxed 2026 conference, the unified, agentic ad platform adds AI-driven Full-Funnel Campaigns and conversational planning tools, letting Amazon's AI decide ad spend allocation across formats for advertisers.

items.headline: TypeSafe says its Jev decision model now used by ~25% of Fortune 500, processing a trillion tokens a day
items.summary: The company credits rapid enterprise adoption to Jev's speed and cost advantages for structured decision tasks, underscoring growing enterprise demand for lightweight, specialized models alongside general-purpose LLMs.

items.headline: Study: Google's AI Mode cuts external clicks without improving user satisfaction
items.summary: A randomized field experiment with 1,100 Chrome users found participants pushed into Google's AI Mode clicked fewer external links, ran fewer search sessions, and reported lower trust and satisfaction than with standard search, adding to concerns about AI search's impact on the open web.
